---
title: "Using an AI assistant"
---

An AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) knows occupancy models and `unmarked`.
What it does not know is this format, and the mistakes it makes because of that
throw no errors. The commonest is turning a missing row into a zero: in eco a
missing row means *not surveyed*, and filling it with 0 biases detection down
and occupancy up. Others are fitting a closed model to occasions the source says
were open, or putting several species in one `unmarked` frame.

The fix is a briefing the assistant reads before it writes code:
[`llms.txt`](llms.txt). It covers the format, the converters, how to find
tables, the defaults that change results, and how to cite: the briefing asks
the assistant to cite the original deposit and paper for every table it uses
(`eco_cite()`), not only eco, and to pass on
[how we ask eco to be used](use.html): respect each table's licence, talk to
the originators before commercial or model-training use, and leave coarsened
coordinates alone. Its counts are regenerated each time the site is built.

## Paste this

Start the conversation with this, followed by your question:

``` text
You are helping me analyse ecological detection data from the eco warehouse.
Before writing any code, fetch and follow
https://ben-domingue.github.io/eco/llms.txt. It documents the data format,
the eco R package, several mistakes that give wrong answers without an
error, and how to cite the original deposits behind each table.

Then help me with: <your question>
```

The assistant fetches the current briefing each time, so there is no copy to
keep up to date.

## If your assistant cannot fetch a URL

Copy the full text below into the conversation instead.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Full text of the briefing

```{r}
#| output: asis
cat("````text\n", paste(readLines("llms.txt", warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n"), "\n````\n", sep = "")
```
:::

## Check what it gives you

The briefing makes the usual mistakes less likely, not impossible. Before you
rely on a fit, check that the detection matrix has `NA` where no survey
happened (`sum(is.na(getY(umf)))` should not be zero for an unbalanced
design), that one species went into each `unmarked` frame, and that the
table's `closure` (in `eco_info()`) suits the model. Each table's processing
script, linked from [the tables page](data.html), says what the source
deposited.
